---
title: "Hierarchical Bayesian TRF model comparison for speech encoding in iEEG"
date: 2026-06-15
description: >
  A formal comparison of two hierarchical Bayesian temporal response function (TRF)
  frameworks for intracranial EEG: a raised-cosine basis model with patient and electrode
  random effects, and a hierarchical Gaussian Process model in which smoothness itself
  varies by patient, electrode and word-level surprisal. Both are compared with standard
  ridge-regression mTRF on held-out predictive accuracy and WAIC/LOO. The question is whether
  prediction error reshapes the neural response through gain control or through predictive coding.
categories: [Bayesian statistics, Neuroscience, Speech ML]
---

Semester research project in the Neural Dynamics Lab, Institute of Neuroinformatics (ETH Zürich),
supervised by Prof. Dr. Timothée Proix, in collaboration with Prof. Dr. Balthasar Bickel (UZH and NCCR).

**Models.** Seven model variants in total, compared on held-out predictive accuracy and on WAIC and
PSIS-LOO. Word-level surprisal from GPT-2 enters as a predictor of the neural response to naturalistic
speech (*The Little Prince* dataset), with an extension to phoneme-level surprisal.

**Validation.** All code (Python: NumPy, SciPy, PyMC, MNE-Python) is validated against synthetic ground
truth at each stage before it touches real data. It will be released on the lab's GitLab.
